prize_parts.citation: for establishing, through quantitative kinetics on photo-triggered redox proteins, how electrons tunnel over long distances through proteins
for the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged in its parts: B058 with Liu alone, and B032 with Gray and Winkler. B058 is the one achievement five of eight members include, and the round-1 exchange did not produce a scientific objection to it, only the shared concerns about the 2020 CRISPR prize and a short clinical record. The chemical content is concrete: an engineered deaminase tethered to a programmable DNA binder, and directed evolution of an adenine deaminase that acts on DNA, which turns base conversion into designed chemistry. Naming Liu alone is defensible because he conceived and led the programme, and the citation can say explicitly that the exclusion of Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida is a consequence of the three-person limit and not a judgement on their work. B032 stands as an experimental discovery. Gray and Winkler's ruthenium-labelled proteins gave the first quantitative, systematic distance and driving-force dependence of electron transfer through a folded polypeptide, and showed that protein structure sets the tunnelling pathway. That is the basis for how respiratory and photosynthetic enzymes move charge, it has been confirmed by many groups for decades, and the credit is two names. I recognise the risk of a two-part prize with no scientific link, and I would accept dropping it if the committee judges that each part cannot stand on its own; I do not think it should be defended as a thematic pairing.
statement.case_against: The strongest case against my configuration is that B032 has the weakest support on the table, and the reservations from Chabes and Sparr, that it confirms a Marcus-type framework already honoured in 1992 in a new medium, have not been answered by any member in my favour. Dutton's empirical tunnelling rules and the 1988 reaction centre prize also sit close to it, and the age of the work means recognition would be late. A two-part prize that joins this to a young genome-editing tool can look like a trade between members, as Somfai, Zou and I have all said. B058 follows CRISPR closely, is about ten years old, and a Liu-only citation leaves out people with strong claims. I also disclose that my own field makes me rate B032 more highly than most colleagues do, and the committee should weight my preference for it accordingly.

responses.point: Chabes argued that B032 is a body of kinetic measurements interpreted within the Marcus framework honoured in 1992, so a prize would partly reward confirmation of theory, and that B008 offers a new mechanism and a general tool; he would accept B032 if argued as an experimental discovery.
responses.response: I accept his condition and I would argue it that way. Marcus predicted a rate dependence on driving force and reorganisation energy for electron transfer in general. He did not predict that a folded polypeptide would behave as a tunnelling medium with a measurable distance decay, nor that the structure would set the coupling pathway. That was settled experimentally in proteins, and it is what lets us calculate electron transfer in enzymes such as cytochrome c oxidase. I still agree that B008 is the stronger candidate on tool-building and impact, which is why it stays my first alternative. My procedural reservation also stands: with eight credited names and no approved degrader, the three-person cut between Crews, Deshaies, Handa and Ciulli has not been resolved, and I would want the expert reports to settle it before I moved it ahead of B058.

responses.point: Sparr said my caveat on B059 changed her view, but she ranks B032 below B064 and B059 because it extends a Marcus-type picture already recognised in 1992 and would be a late recognition of an established area.
responses.response: I agree with her on B059 and have kept it out of my configuration and dropped it as an alternative, since the in vivo function of condensates and the Pappu and Mittag attribution are not settled. On B032 we differ. Lateness alone is not a reason against a result that is stable, quantitatively reproduced and still the working basis for biological electron transfer, and the Nobel record contains many recognitions that came after the field was mature. I do take her point that B064 is a physical-chemical design rule with strong independent evidence, but the Vancouver attribution against MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is exactly the kind of priority dispute I would not want to settle by a three-name cut without the expert reports.

responses.point: The chair proposed pairing B058 with B050 (Bayley and Akeson) as chemically engineered tools that write and read DNA, and asked for each part to be statable to a broad audience, while noting the exclusion of Deamer, Branton and Kasianowicz.
responses.response: His pairing is the more coherent story than mine, and I take the chair's point that a two-part prize should have a one-sentence rationale. My concern is the one he states himself: the credit for nanopore sensing is split between those who proposed strand-through-pore reading, those who made the first demonstration, and those who engineered the pore and the motor enzyme, and a Bayley and Akeson citation leaves out Deamer, Branton and Kasianowicz. I would need the expert reports to show that the engineering is the decisive step before supporting it. I therefore keep B032 as my second part, and I have not moved to B050.

responses.point: Somfai put B030 forward with Buchwald and Hartwig as a mature, clean two-name candidacy and asked what is chemically new in base editing beyond the CRISPR biology already honoured; he also raised Kosugi's tin-amide precursor work.
responses.response: I rate B030 as the strongest of the older candidacies, with the clearest credit, and I now list it as an alternative in place of B059. On his question about B058, the new chemistry is the engineered deaminase acting on DNA, the control of the editing window, and the directed evolution of an adenine deaminase that has no natural DNA activity. Cas9 only cuts, and the base editors do not. I would want the citation to say that. I do not move B030 into my configuration because, as he accepts, the committee may regard it as an extension of the 2010 prize, and I would defer to the synthetic chemists on that.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts a two-part prize in which the parts share no scientific theme, or whether it wants a single coherent achievement.
Whether the expert reports show that B032 is an experimental discovery beyond Marcus (1992) and the 1988 reaction centre prize, and how Dutton's tunnelling rules are credited.
Whether a Liu-only citation for B058 is accepted, or the committee wants Komor and Gaudelli, which would break the three-person limit alongside Gray and Winkler.
Whether the clinical record for base editing is long enough so soon after the 2020 CRISPR prize.
statement.conflict_note: My research on cytochrome c oxidase and on proton and electron transfer in respiratory enzymes is closely related to B032, so I disclose that scientific proximity and have no personal collaboration with Gray or Winkler apparent from my profile. I would defer to colleagues on its relative standing and I have stated openly that my own field raises my regard for it. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, which is not relevant to any shortlisted candidate. No other conflict has arisen from the first round, and no recusal is needed.
